title: rapid tail latency profiling - scratch
content:
Context / goal:
Quick personal scratchpad for a focused tail-latency sweep. Trying to isolate intermittent p99 spikes that users saw on mixed workload (chat + short-embedding). Not full paper — just notes, configs, raw outputs, quick hypotheses and next steps.

Test rig:
- Cluster: dev-gpu-pool-a (4x A100S per node)
- Model: open-llama-13b (int8 quantized build q5_0 + KV cache enabled)
- Runtime: main branch w/ preemptible-eviction fix (PR 842 applied)
- Clients: 16 workers from bench-host-3 (net ~500Mbps to cluster)
- Measure window: 45m per run, collect per-request latencies and traces

Workload patterns tested (arrival distributions):
1) steady poisson at 250 qps (avg tokens/request ~120)
2) bursty: baseline 120 qps + random 1s microbursts to 1200 qps every 30s
3) bimodal: 70% short (20 tokens embeddings style), 30% long-chat (600 tokens) at mixed arrival -> overall 300 qps

Key config knobs:
- batch_timeout_ms: 6 / 12 / 20
- max_batch_tokens: 4096
- kv_cache_prefetch: on/off
- preemption_threshold: 0.85 GPU util cap
- async_io_enabled: true

Selected results (aggregated p50/p95/p99 in ms, run length 45m each):
- Poisson 250 qps, batch_timeout=6ms: p50 42ms, p95 120ms, p99 422ms, qps observed 248
- Poisson 250 qps, batch_timeout=20ms: p50 55ms, p95 180ms, p99 510ms, qps observed 250
- Bursty (microbursts every 30s), timeout=6ms: p50 48ms, p95 210ms, p99 980ms, qps peak 1120
- Bimodal mixed, timeout=6ms, kv_prefetch=on: p50 36ms, p95 160ms, p99 760ms, qps 302
- Bimodal mixed, timeout=6ms, kv_prefetch=off: p50 38ms, p95 180ms, p99 1250ms, qps 299

Observations / quick takeaways:
- Lower batch timeout reduces median but can strongly widen p99 in bursty scenarios — likely more frequent small batches lead to contention for kernel scheduling at high bursts.
- KV cache prefetch materially reduces p99 for mixed short+long workloads (760ms -> 1250ms when off), suggests cache misses during heavy short-request waves cause large tail.
- Increasing batch_timeout to 20ms raised p95/p99 for steady load (more tokens per batch -> slightly higher latency variability), but for bursts it actually smoothed peaks a bit — plausible explanation: larger batches absorb short microbursts, fewer context switches.
- Preemption threshold at 0.85 seems OK; raising to 0.92 reduced p99 during sustained high util but increased average response time (more queuing).

Example per-request tail lines (timestamp, qps_instant, latency_ms, notes):
- 2026-03-09T14:03:12Z, 1180, 2380, "spike coincides with microburst; kernel queue backlog observed in trace"
- 2026-03-09T14:08:24Z, 125, 132, "single long-chat request (600 tokens) — normal"
- 2026-03-09T14:15:41Z, 980, 1110, "kv-miss heavy region, prefetch off"

Things to double-check / hypotheses to test next:
- Hypothesis A: microbursts cause kernel-level scheduler stalls when worker threads oversubscribe streaming multiprocessors (SMs). Need to capture nvprof traces during a controlled microburst.
- Hypothesis B: KV cache eviction policy interacts poorly with mixed request sizes; suggest an experiment with sticky cache pinning for short-embedding requests.
- Hypothesis C: batching windows + async IO interplay — run a matrix where async_io toggled against batch_timeout in both steady and burst modes.

Quick action items:
- [ ] Re-run microburst experiment with nvprof traces enabled for 5 bursts (assign to Rohit)
- [ ] Add lightweight sampling at 1% of requests to capture stack traces and full kernel schedule timeline (assign to Maya)
- [ ] Try sticky cache pin for top-10 most frequent embeddings keys for 30m run (I will sketch config)
- [ ] Open follow-up ticket documenting p99->kv_prefetch correlation and propose prefetch-by-pattern.

Notes to self:
- Keep runs short-ish (30-60m) but repeat across different times of day to catch infra noise.
- Share preliminary numbers in #eng-runtime with brief bullets, include graphs from bench host (I have CSVs in bench-host-3:/tmp/bench-20260309).
- Don't conflate p99 due to model compute vs p99 due to infra/network — trace fields are crucial.

Unresolved questions:
- Is there any interplay with host-level cgroups that causes stalls when multiple containers spike simultaneously? (SRE to check node-level metrics)
- Are the p99 events correlated with other tenants on the same node (noisy neighbor)? Need node allocation logs.

References / links:
- JIRA: JIRA-RW-2719 (investigate intermittent p99 in prod-like load)
- PR with preemption fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- Slack snippets: #runtime (thread "today's microburst run")

Closing note: This scratch is a running ledger — will merge useful distilled notes into a short postmortem if Rohit reproduces kernel scheduling pattern. For now: kv-prefetch looks like the lowest-effort mitigation for mixed workload tails.

-- Harper
